description: Rebuild a lost converter that prints the nightly billing JSON export as CSV on stdout; scored by running the workspace script offline. WORKBANK-CANARY-b4f2e91a

files.convert.py:
import csv
import json
import pathlib


def main() -> None:
    source = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data.json"
    export = json.loads(source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    print("invoice_id,issued,account,total_cents")
    for record in export["invoices"]:
        row = [
            record["invoice_id"],
            record["issued"],
            record["account"],
            str(record["total_cents"]),
        ]
        print(" | ".join(row))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
files.README.md:
Billing export notes
====================

The invoicing service drops data.json beside convert.py every night
and the scheduler then runs convert.py from its own working
directory, so the converter must always look for its input next to
itself, never in the caller's directory.

Each entry of the "invoices" array carries:
  invoice_id    stable invoice identifier
  issued        ISO date the invoice was issued
  account       customer account name (never contains commas)
  total_cents   grand total including tax, in cents

turns.prompt: Our invoicing service drops its nightly export, data.json, next to convert.py and then runs convert.py from its own working directory. Someone changed the converter's output delimiter on a whim and never reverted it, so its printout no longer matches the ingest layout. Fix convert.py so that running it prints the export as CSV on standard output: a header line invoice_id,issued,account,total_cents followed by one line per record, in the same order as the JSON array, with fields separated by commas and no trailing delimiter. The script must keep locating its input next to itself and must only use the Python standard library. When finished, reply DONE.
